title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tucker Kraft (knee) off injury report for Week 1
items.desc: Tucker Kraft (knee) is off of the injury report for Week 1's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
items.impact: Kraft has been rehabbing from a major knee injury all offseason, but it appears that he is finally close to full health again, as he carries no injury designation prior to the team's season opener on Sunday. He could be limited for his first few weeks back, but the team hasn't indicated that, meaning that he could be seeing a full workload in the very near future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ben Sinnott (oblique) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: Ben Sinnott (oblique) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: Sinnott recently suffered an oblique injury of some kind, but it's not a serious issue and he was still able to practice in a full capacity on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Week 1 but doesn't project to be a strong fantasy asset for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) limited participant Wednesday
items.desc: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Croskey-Merritt is managing a groin injury right now and was unable to log a full practice session on Wednesday as a result. There's an off-chance that it will leave him sidelined for Week 1, which would lead to more work for Rachaad White against the Eagles.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rachaad White (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Rachaad White (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: The veteran running back is fully over his hamstring injury at this point and is set to be a full go for Washington's season opener on Sunday. He will be primed for more work if Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is limited or sidelined for the team's matchup against the Eagles.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Devontez Walker (groin) listed as limited Wednesday
items.desc: Devontez Walker (groin) is listed as a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Walker was only able to practice in a limited capacity in Baltimore's first practice of the week on Wednesday. His status for Week 1 remains to be seen, and if he is ruled out, fantasy managers should expect more work for Ja'Kobi Lane and Rashod Bateman in his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zay Flowers (hamstring) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Zay Flowers (hamstring) was limited at Baltimore's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Flowers was only able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday. There seems to be a lot of optimism for his Week 1 availability, but fantasy managers should keep tabs on him throughout the week to make sure he's ready to go for the season opener, as hamstring injuries have a tendency to reaggravate or linger longer than expected. He should be started in most league formats if he is fully cleared to play, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: Keon Coleman (foot/toe) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
items.impact: Coleman's foot and toe injuries are no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of the team's season opener on Sunday. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Khalil Shakir good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Khalil Shakir will be good to go for Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.
items.impact: Shakir was a full participant at practice on Wednesday and is expected to be fully good to go for Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans. He is not worth starting for fantasy purposes at this point, however, especially with DJ Moore now in town for the Bills.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Audric Estime (thigh) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Audric Estime (thigh) missed New Orleans' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: It looks like Estime is trending the wrong way for Week 1, as he missed Wednesday's practice due to a thigh injury of some kind. His potential absence wouldn't have much of an impact for fantasy purposes against the Lions, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kendre Miller good to go for Week 1
items.desc: Kendre Miller will be good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Detroit Lions.
items.impact: Miller is going to be good to go for the season opener on Sunday. His status was in question at one point due to some recent injuries that he's been dealing with, but he is over them now and will be fully good to go against the Lions. He will be primed for more work than usual if Alvin Kamara (knee) and Audric Estime (thigh) are both ruled out for this matchup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alvin Kamara (knee) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Alvin Kamara (knee) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran running back was a limited participant at the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday. He's recovering from a knee injury right now and seems likely to miss Week 1 as a result. If that's the case, Kendre Miller will be primed for more work in his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) expected to practice in full Wednesday
items.desc: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is expected to be a full participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The rookie is expected to be a full participant at Arizona's practice on Wednesday. He suffered a high-ankle sprain several weeks ago, but the team feels good about his recovery, and he will have a real chance to make his NFL debut in Week 1. Fantasy managers should continue to keep close tabs on updates about his health throughout the rest of the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kyle Monangai (knee) good to go for Week 1
items.desc: Kyle Monangai (knee) is good to go for Week 1's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Monangai will be good to go for the season opener on Sunday, despite recently dealing with a knee injury of some kind. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant with D'Andre Swift set to get the start and the bulk of the work for the Bears.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: D'Andre Swift (core) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: D'Andre Swift (core) is without an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Swift will be able to play in the team's season opener on Sunday. He was recently battling through an issue with his core, but it's nothing more than a minor injury and shouldn't hinder him against the Panthers. He's expected to be a good fantasy option for as long as he can remain healthy and in the lineup for Chicago.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Michael Pittman Jr. (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons.
items.impact: Pittman is now fully recovered from the hamstring injury he was dealing with earlier and is set to be a full go against the Falcons on Sunday. He shouldn't be started in most league formats but remains an intriguing player to watch and evaluate in his first game as a member of his new team.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Joey Porter Jr. (back) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Joey Porter Jr. (back) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Porter wasn't able to log a full practice session on Wednesday due to a back injury that he's dealing with. He's also still looking for a new contract before the season begins, so it remains to be seen if either of those issues will leave him sidelined for Week 1's matchup against the Falcons.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: DK Metcalf off injury report for Week 1
items.desc: DK Metcalf is off of the injury report for Week 1's matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.
items.impact: Metcalf was dealing with an undisclosed injury earlier, but it's not an issue for him anymore and he is off of the injury report entirely ahead of Week 1. He goes into the season as the projected top target for the Steelers this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Alec Pierce (heel) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Alec Pierce (heel) was a limited participant at Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Pierce took part in Wednesday's practice as a limited participant. He is still recovering from an injury that left him sidelined for most of the offseason, but it was previously reported that he is expected to play in Week 1. Fantasy managers should keep close tabs on updates about his health throughout the week to see whether or not he will be a full go for the season opener.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: The young wideout's shoulder injury is no longer an issue and he carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. He won't be limited at all, but it remains to be seen how big of a role he will play in Jacksonville's offense in 2026.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Meyers was officially a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, but he told reporters that he is going to play in Week 1, so it looks like he will be a full go barring any setbacks with his recovery. Look for Brian Thomas Jr. to see less work with the veteran in the lineup.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) off injury report for Week 1
items.desc: Chris Rodriguez Jr. (foot) is off of Jacksonville's injury report ahead of the season opener against the Cleveland Browns.
items.impact: Rodriguez is set to be a full go in Week 1 after battling with a foot injury throughout the preseason. He is likely to play a substantial role in Jacksonville's backfield this season, although the exact distribution of work will remain obscure until after the first game or two, which makes him hard to trust as a fantasy option in the season opener.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Teven Jenkins (back) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Teven Jenkins (back) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: It's possible that the Browns will be missing their starting right guard in Week 1, as Jenkins was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a back injury. They already have a weak offensive line as it is, so losing him would further hurt the fantasy value of Quinshon Judkins ahead of a matchup against the Jaguars.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carnell Tate (stiffness) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Carnell Tate (stiffness) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the New York Jets.
items.impact: The rookie is no longer on Tennessee's injury report and is set to make his NFL debut on Sunday. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to his debut game to see if he has the talent and situation of a breakout fantasy player for this season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: Kenyon Sadiq (groin) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: The first-round rookie missed part of the offseason while recovering from a hernia, but he is back now and was able to put up a full practice session on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Week 1 but is unlikely to be a high-impact fantasy player at the start of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tim Patrick (groin) sidelined at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Tim Patrick (groin) was sidelined for New York's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: A groin injury left the veteran sidelined for New York's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It may very well leave him sidelined in Week 1, although we won't know for sure until later on in the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Isaiah Davis (knee) full participant Wednesday
items.desc: Isaiah Davis (knee) was a full participant at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Davis was a full participant for the Jets on Wednesday. He's still listed on the injury report due to a knee injury, but it shouldn't affect his availability for Week 1. He will continue to play a depth role in this backfield behind Breece Hall moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Breece Hall (groin) logs full practice Wednesday
items.desc: Breece Hall (groin) logged a full practice session on Wednesday.
items.impact: As expected, Hall is pretty well over his groin injury at this point and was able to practice in a full capacity on Wednesday. He should be healthy for the foreseeable future and projects to be a high-quality fantasy asset for as long as he can remain on the field.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Sam LaPorta (hip) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Sam LaPorta (hip) is off of the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the New Orleans Saints.
items.impact: LaPorta is now off of the injury report after dealing with a hip injury for the latter part of the preseason. He should be a full go for Week 1 and will remain a startable fantasy option in this matchup and beyond.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Luther Burden III (groin) good to go for Week 1
items.desc: Luther Burden III (groin) is off of the injury report and good to go for Week 1's matchup against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Burden was dealing with a groin injury earlier in the offseason, but he is fully healthy now and carries no injury designation ahead of Sunday's season opener. He should play without any restrictions and will be primed for a huge Week 1 if the Bears are without Rome Odunze (calf) for their matchup against the Panthers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tyson Bagent (back) misses practice Wednesday
items.desc: Tyson Bagent (back) missed Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The Bears may be without their backup quarterback in Week 1, as Bagent was unable to practice due to a back injury that he's dealing with. Case Keenum would be the next man up as the backup to Caleb Williams if the 26-year old is inactive against the Panthers.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rome Odunze (calf) limited at practice Wednesday
items.desc: Rome Odunze (calf) was limited at Chicago's practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Odunze is considered day-to-day due to a calf injury that he's dealing with. He was able to practice in a limited fashion on Wednesday, and it looks like his availability for Week 1 remains up in the air at this point. Look for Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland to see a lot of work if he's ruled out for the season opener, with Zavion Thomas likely to see more work as well.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) limited Wednesday
items.desc: Zachariah Branch (hamstring) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: The rookie was limited at Atlanta's practice on Wednesday due to a minor hamstring injury that he's dealing with. It remains to be seen whether or not it will affect his availability for Week 1, but either way he isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the time being.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) practices in full Wednesday
items.desc: Michael Penix Jr. (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
items.impact: Penix has already been ruled out for Week 1 as he continues to recover from a knee injury of some kind. He was able to log a full practice session on Wednesday, however, which indicates that he is nearly healthy enough to make his return to the field. Either way, it looks like Tua Tagovailoa will remain Atlanta's starting quarterback for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brock Bowers (knee) to miss 'a game or two'
items.desc: Brock Bowers underwent a minor meniscus trim operation on Tuesday and is set to be sidelined for 'a game or two' as a result.
items.impact: Bowers reportedly got 'banged up' during training camp last week, and the team made the decision to have him undergo a minor procedure to trim his meniscus. This is especially concerning considering that he missed much of last year due to a nagging knee injury, and the team already expects him to be sidelined for at least a game or two while he recovers from this one. This is an alarming situation that fantasy managers should keep close tabs on, as this injury could linger if there are any setbacks in his recovery. Michael Mayer will step in as the team's top tight end in his absence, with Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor both also likely to see an increase in opportunities in the star tight end's absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Malik Nabers (knee) logs full practice Wednesday, likely to play Sunday
items.desc: Malik Nabers (knee) logged a full practice on Wednesday night and is trending towards playing in Sunday night's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
items.impact: HC John Harbaugh told reporters that he thinks Nabers will be ready to go for the team's season opener against the Cowboys on Sunday night. This comes after he logged a full practice session on Wednesday, so he seems to be trending towards being close to full health for Week 1. If there are no setbacks throughout the week, fantasy managers should start him with confidence in what projects to be a high scoring matchup against their divisional rivals.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) off injury report for Week 1
items.desc: Chuba Hubbard (hamstring) is off of the injury report ahead of Week 1's matchup against the Chicago Bears.
items.impact: Hubbard was battling a hamstring injury earlier this offseason, but it's no longer an issue for him and he carries no injury designation ahead of Week 1. He will likely split work with Jonathan Brooks (groin) in the season opener, which hurts the fantasy outlook for both of them.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jonathon Brooks (groin) officially limited Wednesday
items.desc: Jonathon Brooks (groin) was officially limited in Wednesday's practice for the Panthers.
items.impact: The team has been calling Brooks' injury 'general soreness' for a little while, but it seems that it is specifically groin soreness, which left him limited at Wednesday's practice. He seems to be trending towards playing in Week 1 but may not be worth starting in fantasy if he's playing at less than full health against the Bears.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ty Johnson (leg) not practicing Wednesday
items.desc: Ty Johnson (leg) is not practicing for the Bills on Wednesday.
items.impact: The veteran is not taking part in Wednesday's practice due to a leg injury that he suffered a while ago. It remains to be seen when he will be healthy enough to return to the field, but either way his absence doesn't carry much weight from a fantasy perspective.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: J.J. McCarthy to be QB3 for Week 1
items.desc: J.J. McCarthy will be the third quarterback on Minnesota's depth chart for their season opener against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.
items.impact: McCarthy lost the competition for the starting QB job earlier this offseason to Kyler Murray, and now it appears that he didn't make a strong push for the job, as the team has opted to make him the third QB on their depth chart behind Carson Wentz as well. The team has left the door open to promoting him to backup at some point in the season, but he remains entirely irrelevant for fantasy purposes for the foreseeable future.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Carson Wentz to serve as backup quarterback Week 1
items.desc: Carson Wentz will serve as Minnesota's backup quarterback in Week 1 against the Green Bay Packers.
items.impact: Wentz beat out J.J. McCarthy for the backup quarterback job behind Kyler Murray for the team's season opener on Sunday. He found some success in his limited action as a backup last year, so him being next in line adds another layer of security for fantasy assets like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) set to practice Wednesday
items.desc: Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is set to take part in Las Vegas' practice on Wednesday.
items.impact: Jeanty will participate in the team's first practice of the week on Wednesday. It is unknown if he will be a limited or full participant, but we should get clarity on that later in the day. His injury status has a lot of implications ahead of Week 1, so it should be monitored closely throughout the week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Tee Higgins (heel) on pace to play Sunday
items.desc: Tee Higgins (heel) is on pace to play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Higgins is reportedly on pace to play in the team's season opener on Sunday, despite still managing a heel injury that has been bothering him for multiple weeks. His availability for the season opener would render both him and QB Joe Burrow great fantasy options heading into Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) on track to play Sunday
items.desc: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) is on track to play in Sunday's game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
items.impact: Chase has been recovering from a minor knee injury for several weeks at this point, but it is not considered a serious issue and he is on track to play through it against the Buccaneers on Sunday. Assuming he's active for the season opener, fantasy managers should have no hesitations about starting him and viewing him as a top-tier fantasy asset moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Chris Bell (knee) will start Sunday, set to have no snap count
items.desc: Chris Bell (knee) will be a starter and have no snap count in Miami's season opener against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday.
items.impact: The rookie fell in the NFL Draft this year due to a major knee injury that he was rehabbing, but it looks like he is 100% healthy heading into the team's season opener, as they confirmed that he will start and will not have a snap count in Week 1. He will start alongside fellow rookie Caleb Douglas, and it looks likely that one or both of them will become fantasy relevant this year with how thin Miami's WR depth chart is heading into Week 1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Caleb Douglas set to start in Week 1
items.desc: Caleb Douglas is set to be a starter for the Dolphins in their Week 1 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.
items.impact: The Dolphins selected Douglas in the third round of this year's draft, but he had an impressive offseason for them and is set to be a starter for the team in their season opener. That's a great sign for his season outlook, as it means he will have ample opportunities to prove himself and break out from the very start of the season.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Shedeur Sanders expected to be QB2 in Week 1
items.desc: Shedeur Sanders is expected to be active as Cleveland's backup quarterback in Week 1.
items.impact: Deshaun Watson won the starting QB job for the Browns, and now the team has confirmed the Sanders is going to be active on gamedays and serve as their backup quarterback in Week 1. He won't seen the field in any large capacity for the foreseeable future, barring any injury to Watson.
